summary:
Nord-Ovest bundles Italy's two most protective municipal measures for transgender people with two of the six highest-victim regions in the Progetto Gionata dataset. Milano operates Italy's first "registro di genere" (chosen name on civic documents, transport subscriptions, staff badges) and Torino runs "Identita Alias" at the comune and public libraries - practical tools that determine whether a gender-nonconforming visitor is humiliated at a ticket window or not. Against this, Lombardy and Piedmont are named as high-violence regions; a 28-year-old trans woman was found dead in Alessandria (Oct 2025), linked to a robbery series targeting vulnerable people, and right-wing militants gave Roman salutes along the Brianza Pride route (Sept 2025).

The institutional responses are notably good: the Carabinieri scientific section produced prompt charges with wiretaps and confessions in the Alessandria killing; the Digos moved pre-emptively at Brianza Pride and "struck out at birth" the spark. Lombardy's 2015 "natural family" motion and rejection of WHO sex-ed standards are dated climate signals with no visitor-facing enforcement mechanism.

Net deviation: -0.03 from the national score (0.50). The violence concentration is real for a traveler, but the protective registries and the quality of institutional responses partially offset it. Compared to Centro (0.52), this unit lacks a landmark transphobic-motive conviction but has more practical visitor-facing protections and more documented violence. Compared to Nord-Est (0.47), the protective measures here are concrete and used, not merely symbolic motions.

sources.summary: LifeGate report: Milano city council approved the first "registro di genere" in Italy (motion by Monica Romano, the first transgender woman elected to the council, 2022), granting a chosen name on civic and municipal documents, public-transport subscriptions and staff badges; Torino introduced the analogous "Identita Alias" practice at the comune and public libraries. These are the practical, visitor-facing administrative tools named in the dossier for this unit.

Progetto Gionata region-by-region study of anti-LGBT hate-motivated violence 2012-2025: names the six Italian regions with the highest victim counts; Lombardia and Piemonte (both inside Nord-Ovest) are two of the six, alongside Lazio and Toscana (Centro), Campania and Puglia (Sud). Basis of the high-violence attribution for this unit.

Torino Cronaca report: a 28-year-old transgender woman was found dead in her flat in Alessandria (via De Amicis) on 9 October 2025; on 22 December 2025 the Carabinieri scientific section charged and jailed two men aged 22 and 25 - already imprisoned for a series of violent robberies against vulnerable people - linking them to the killing through wiretaps and a confession. Recorded as a prompt, well-run institutional response inside a documented robbery pattern targeting fragile people.

MB News report (27 September 2025): right-wing militants were filmed giving Roman salutes along the Brianza Pride parade route at Arcore; the Digos political police moved pre-emptively against the organisers and reported the attack "struck out at birth" - an attempted anti-Pride action neutralised before it escalated.

tangentialFactors: Lombardy's 2015 regional-council motion "in support of the natural family" and against "gender ideology", and the region's rejection of WHO sexuality-education standards, are a durable political-climate signal against LGBT+ rights generally, with no visitor-facing enforcement mechanism.
